title: The Second Book of Chronicles Timeline
sub: Solomon's Temple to the Exile · Judah's Story, Priestly Eyes
desc: Skipping the northern kingdom almost entirely, the Chronicler follows only Judah's kings from Solomon's temple-building through faithful reformers like Asa, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, and Josiah, to the temple's destruction — and closes, remarkably, on a note of hope: Cyrus's decree to rebuild.

eras.label: Era One · 2 Chronicles 1
eras.name: Solomon's Wisdom at Gibeon
eras.dates: The Chronicler opens Solomon's reign with the same dream at Gibeon told in 1 Kings — wisdom requested over wealth, and both granted — but skips straight past the two-prostitutes judgment scene to Solomon's growing wealth. (Hebrew verse 18 is numbered as most English Bibles' 2:1.)

events.title: "Give Me Wisdom and Discernment"
events.detail: At the Gibeon worship center, God offers Solomon anything he wants; Solomon asks for wisdom and discernment to lead the nation rather than riches or vengeance on his enemies, and receives both the wisdom he requested and the wealth he did not ask for.

verses.text: “God [Elohim] said to Solomon, ‘Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth, riches, and honor… but you asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge my people… wisdom and knowledge is given to you, and I will give you wealth and riches and honor such as no king before you has had, and none after you will have.’”

events.title: Chariots, Horses, and Silver Like Stone
events.detail: Solomon accumulates 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, makes silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as ordinary stones, and orders the temple to be built. (Numbered 2:1 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Two · 2 Chronicles 2
eras.name: Preparing to Build — the Message to Huram
eras.dates: Solomon writes to Huram of Tyre for both materials and a master craftsman, explaining that the temple's true purpose is worship, not to house a God the heavens themselves cannot contain. (Hebrew chapter 2 begins at what most English Bibles number as 2:2.)

events.title: "Our God Is Greater Than All Gods"
events.detail: Solomon requests cedar, a skilled craftsman, and enormous quantities of wheat, barley, wine, and oil from Huram of Tyre, explaining the temple is not truly a house that could contain God but a place to offer sacrifices; Huram responds by sending Huram Abi, a master craftsman, and blessing the LORD for giving David "a wise son." (Numbered 2:2-18 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “I will build a great temple, for our God is greater than all gods. Of course, who can really build a temple for him, since the sky and the highest heavens cannot contain him? Who am I that I should build him a temple!”

eras.label: Era Three · 2 Chronicles 3
eras.name: The Temple's Foundation and Interior
eras.dates: Construction begins at the exact site of David's altar on Mount Moriah — Ornan's threshing floor — and the interior is finished in gold-plated cedar with two enormous cherubim spanning the Most Holy Place wall to wall.

events.title: Building on Mount Moriah
events.detail: Solomon builds on Mount Moriah, at the very site David had prepared at Ornan's threshing floor, overlaying the interior in gold, carving cherubim on the walls, and setting up two bronze pillars named Jakin and Boaz at the entrance.

eras.label: Era Four · 2 Chronicles 4
eras.name: The Bronze Sea and the Temple's Furnishings
eras.dates: Huram Abi casts the massive bronze Sea on twelve bulls along with the altar, basins, and lampstands, in quantities so vast that Solomon simply stopped weighing the bronze.

events.title: Furnishing the Temple
events.detail: Huram Abi casts the bronze Sea resting on twelve bulls, ten bronze basins and ten gold lampstands, and every other item Solomon assigned him — so much bronze in total that "they did not weigh" it.

verses.text: “Solomon made so many of these items they did not weigh the bronze.”

eras.label: Era Five · 2 Chronicles 5
eras.name: The Ark Installed — the Cloud Fills the Temple
eras.dates: The ark's arrival becomes an occasion for a unified blast of praise from every trumpeter and singer, and the cloud that fills the temple in response makes the priests unable to continue their service.

events.title: "Certainly He Is Good" — the Cloud Fills the House
events.detail: The ark of the covenant is carried into the Most Holy Place beneath the cherubim's wings; when trumpeters and singers unite "as one" to praise the LORD, a cloud fills the temple so completely the priests cannot continue their service.

verses.text: “The trumpeters and singers played together as one, praising and giving thanks to the LORD [Yahweh]… ‘Certainly he is good; certainly his loyal love endures!’ Then a cloud filled the LORD's [Yahweh] temple. The priests could not carry out their duties because of the cloud.”

eras.label: Era Six · 2 Chronicles 6
eras.name: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication
eras.dates: Kneeling on a specially built bronze platform before the whole assembly, Solomon prays through seven scenarios in which Israel — or even a distant foreigner — might cry out for God's help, opening with the flat declaration that no god anywhere compares.

events.title: "The LORD Has Kept the Promise"
events.detail: Solomon blesses the assembly, recounting how the LORD chose Jerusalem and David and has now fulfilled his promise through the completed temple.

events.title: "There Is No God Like You" — Seven Petitions
events.detail: Kneeling on a bronze platform before the entire assembly, Solomon prays that God hear Israel from heaven in seven scenarios — a false oath, military defeat, drought, famine, the foreigner's prayer, war, and exile — closing with a request that God rise to his resting place and never reject his anointed one.

verses.text: “O LORD [Yahweh], the God [Elohim] of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven or on earth! You maintain covenantal loyalty to your servants who obey you with sincerity.”
“God [Elohim] does not really live with humankind on the earth! Look, if the sky and the highest heaven cannot contain you, how much less this temple I have built!”

eras.label: Era Seven · 2 Chronicles 7
eras.name: Fire From Heaven — the LORD's Second Appearance
eras.dates: Fire falling visibly from the sky to consume Solomon's sacrifice becomes this book's own confirming sign — absent from Kings' account — before the LORD appears to Solomon a second time with the same conditional promise given every king after him.

events.title: Fire Falls; the Splendor Fills the Temple
events.detail: As soon as Solomon finishes praying, fire falls from heaven and consumes the sacrifice while the LORD's splendor fills the temple so completely the priests cannot enter; the dedication festival runs a full two weeks, and the people go home "happy and contented."

verses.text: “When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the LORD's [Yahweh] splendor filled the temple.”

events.title: "If My People… Will Humble Themselves"
events.detail: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time with the same conditional covenant given through the whole historical narrative — obedience secures the dynasty, but abandonment means exile and a temple reduced to a byword — including the verse that becomes one of the most quoted in the book.

verses.text: “And my people, who bear my name, humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and forgive their sin and heal their land.”

eras.label: Era Eight · 2 Chronicles 8-9
eras.name: Solomon's Building Projects, and the Queen of Sheba
eras.dates: Solomon expands his kingdom's infrastructure and wealth to a scale the Chronicler treats as self-evidently the reward of faithfulness, capped by a foreign queen's overwhelmed testimony to his God-given wisdom.

events.title: Cities, Fleets, and Faithful Worship
events.detail: Solomon builds fortified cities, organizes his workforce so Israelites serve only as soldiers and officers rather than laborers, keeps the full sacrificial calendar exactly as Moses prescribed, and sends ships to Ophir that return with 450 talents of gold.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba's Visit, and Solomon's Wealth
events.detail: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and leaves overwhelmed, confessing the reports she heard did not tell half the story; the chapter closes cataloging his gold income, ivory throne, and horses before his forty-year reign ends and Rehoboam succeeds him.

verses.text: “May the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] be blessed, who has delighted in you to put you on his throne as king for the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] — because your God [Elohim] loves Israel, to establish it forever, he has appointed you over them as king to do justice and righteousness.”

eras.label: Era Nine · 2 Chronicles 10
eras.name: The Kingdom Splits
eras.dates: Rehoboam's harsh response to Israel's request for lighter labor fractures the united kingdom permanently — the same episode 1 Kings tells, with the Chronicler making explicit that the outcome was God's own doing.

events.title: "My Father Disciplined You With Whips"
events.detail: Rehoboam rejects the elders' moderate counsel for his peers' harsh one, and ten tribes revolt under Jeroboam, leaving Rehoboam only Judah — a rupture the text attributes directly to God "instigating this turn of events" to fulfill his earlier word through Ahijah.

verses.text: “The king refused to listen to the people, because God was instigating this turn of events so that he might bring to pass the prophetic announcement he had made through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.”

eras.label: Era Ten · 2 Chronicles 11-12
eras.name: Rehoboam's Fortifications, and Shishak's Invasion
eras.dates: Rehoboam builds a network of fortified cities and welcomes priests fleeing Jeroboam's idolatry, but his own unfaithfulness invites an Egyptian invasion that only his last-minute humility manages to soften.

events.title: Fortified Cities, and Priests Who Flee to Judah
events.detail: Rehoboam is stopped from attacking Israel by a direct prophetic word declaring the split God's own doing, then fortifies fifteen cities throughout Judah and Benjamin; priests and Levites loyal to the LORD abandon Jeroboam's territory entirely rather than serve his golden calves.

verses.text: “The LORD says this: ‘Do not attack and make war with your brothers. Each of you go home, for I have caused this to happen.’”

events.title: Shishak's Invasion, and a Humbled King Spared
events.detail: Once Rehoboam's rule is secure, he and Judah abandon the LORD's law, and Shishak of Egypt invades and strips Jerusalem's treasures; only when Rehoboam and the leaders humble themselves does the prophet Shemaiah announce partial mercy — Judah survives, though as Shishak's subjects, "to experience how serving me differs from serving the surrounding nations."

verses.text: “When the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, the LORD's message came to Shemaiah: ‘They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them… Yet they will become his subjects, so they can experience how serving me differs from serving the surrounding nations.’”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 2 Chronicles 13
eras.name: Abijah's War Against Jeroboam
eras.dates: Outnumbered two to one and ambushed front and back, Abijah's army wins decisively after a mid-battle cry to the LORD — a chapter with no parallel emphasis in Kings, where Abijah otherwise receives a largely negative review. (Hebrew verse 23 — Abijah's death — is numbered as most English Bibles' 14:1.)

events.title: Ambushed, Then Delivered by a Battle Cry
events.detail: Facing an Israelite army twice the size of his own and ambushed from front and rear, Abijah's forces cry out to the LORD mid-battle; God strikes down Jeroboam's army before them, resulting in 500,000 Israelite casualties and several captured cities, with the text crediting the victory explicitly to Judah's reliance on the LORD.

verses.text: “As for us, the LORD is our God and we have not forsaken him… Now look, God is with us as our leader. His priests are ready to blow the trumpets to signal the attack against you. Do not fight against the LORD God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed!”

events.title: Abijah's Death
events.detail: Abijah dies and is buried in the City of David, and his son Asa replaces him as king, opening a decade of rest for the land. (Numbered 14:1 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Twelve · 2 Chronicles 14-15
eras.name: Asa's Reforms and Victory Over Zerah
eras.dates: Asa tears down the high places his predecessors left standing, prays a short, urgent battle prayer against an overwhelming Cushite army, and responds to a prophet's encouragement with a nationwide covenant renewal.

events.title: Reform and a Decade of Rest
events.detail: Asa removes pagan altars and high places, orders Judah to seek the LORD, and enjoys ten years of peace to fortify his cities — attributed directly to his faithfulness. (Numbered 14:2-8 in most English translations.)

events.title: "There Is No One But You" — Victory Over a Million-Man Army
events.detail: Facing Zerah the Cushite's army of a million men, Asa prays a short, desperate prayer trusting in the LORD alone, and the army is routed so completely that Judah's men spend days hauling off plunder from the surrounding towns. (Numbered 14:9-15 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “Asa prayed to the LORD his God: ‘O LORD [Yahweh], there is no one but you who can help the weak when they are vastly outnumbered. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on you.’” (Numbered 14:11 in most English translations.)

events.title: "If You Seek Him, He Will Respond" — Covenant Renewal
events.detail: The prophet Azariah tells Asa the LORD is with him only "when you are loyal to him," and Asa responds by removing his own grandmother from her position for idolatry and leading a solemn covenant to seek the LORD wholeheartedly, on penalty of death for anyone who refused.

verses.text: “He said to him, ‘Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin! The LORD [Yahweh] is with you when you are with him, and if you seek him, he will let himself be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.’”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 2 Chronicles 16
eras.name: Asa's Later Failure — Trust in Syria Instead of the LORD
eras.dates: The same king who once prayed "there is no one but you" against a million-man army later strips the temple treasury to buy Syrian help against a much smaller threat — and imprisons the prophet who calls him on it.

events.title: "You Relied on the King of Syria"
events.detail: Asa buys Ben Hadad of Syria's help against Baasha with temple silver rather than trusting the LORD as he had against the Cushites; the prophet Hanani rebukes him directly, and Asa jails him in anger rather than repent — later refusing to seek the LORD even for a severe foot disease that eventually kills him.

verses.text: “The LORD's [Yahweh] eyes are roving throughout the earth to show himself strong for those whose heart is completely his. You have acted foolishly in this matter; from now on you will have wars.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 2 Chronicles 17
eras.name: Jehoshaphat's Faithful Reign
eras.dates: Jehoshaphat's reign opens with a rare, explicit program of religious education — officials and Levites sent throughout Judah's cities with the scroll of the law itself, a detail found nowhere else in the historical books.

events.title: Teaching the Law Throughout Judah
events.detail: Jehoshaphat removes high places and Asherah poles, and in a detail unique to Chronicles, sends officials, Levites, and priests throughout every city of Judah carrying the scroll of the law itself to teach the people — resulting in such respect from surrounding nations that none dare make war on him.

verses.text: “They taught throughout Judah, taking with them the scroll of the law of the LORD. They traveled to all the cities of Judah and taught the people.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 2 Chronicles 18
eras.name: Micaiah and the Death of Ahab
eras.dates: Allied by marriage with Ahab's house, Jehoshaphat nearly dies in a battle he was warned against by the one true prophet present — the same Micaiah episode told in 1 Kings 22, almost word for word.

events.title: Four Hundred False Prophets, and One True One
events.detail: Allied with Ahab by marriage, Jehoshaphat joins an attack on Ramoth Gilead despite Micaiah's lone prophecy of disaster among 400 court prophets predicting victory; Ahab dies from a random arrow exactly as foretold, while Jehoshaphat survives an assault meant for the king of Israel only because he cries out and the LORD draws his attackers away.

verses.text: “When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, ‘It is the king of Israel!’ and they surrounded him to do battle. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him — God lured them away from him.”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 2 Chronicles 19
eras.name: Jehoshaphat's Judicial Reforms
eras.dates: Rebuked by a prophet for allying with Ahab, Jehoshaphat responds by establishing a court system explicitly framed as serving the LORD rather than mere human interests — judges warned that bribery and partiality are personally offensive to God.

events.title: "You Are Not Judging for Men, but for the LORD"
events.detail: Rebuked for allying with wicked Ahab, Jehoshaphat responds by touring the kingdom to encourage faithfulness and appointing judges in every fortified city, charging them that their decisions are made in the LORD's presence and that God "disapproves of injustice, partiality, and bribery."

verses.text: “He told the judges, ‘Be careful what you do, for you are not judging for men, but for the LORD, who will be with you when you make judicial decisions. Respect the LORD and make careful decisions, for the LORD our God disapproves of injustice, partiality, and bribery.’”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · 2 Chronicles 20
eras.name: Invasion Repelled by a Choir Marching Into Battle
eras.dates: Facing a coalition of Moab, Ammon, and Edom, Jehoshaphat's entire strategy is prayer and worship — he sends singers, not soldiers, to the front of the army, and the enemy destroys itself before Judah ever draws a sword.

events.title: "The Battle Is Not Yours, But God's"
events.detail: Facing an invading coalition, Jehoshaphat leads all Judah in fasting and a long public prayer, ending simply "we look to you for help"; the LORD's Spirit comes on the Levite Jachaziel, who promises the battle belongs entirely to God and that Judah need only "take your positions, stand, and watch."

verses.text: “He said, ‘Pay attention, all you people of Judah, residents of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! This is what the LORD [Yahweh] says to you: Don't be afraid and don't panic because of this huge army, for the battle is not yours, but God's [Elohim].’”

events.title: Singers Sent Ahead of the Army
events.detail: Jehoshaphat appoints musicians to march at the front of the army singing "Give thanks to the LORD, for his loyal love endures"; the moment they begin praising, the LORD sets the invading coalition against itself so completely that Judah finds only corpses and three days' worth of plunder waiting for them.

verses.text: “Trust in the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] and you will be safe! Trust in the message of his prophets and you will win.”
“When they began to shout and praise, the LORD [Yahweh] suddenly attacked the Ammonites, Moabites, and men from Mount Seir who were invading Judah, and they were defeated.”

events.title: Jehoshaphat's Reign Summarized, and a Wrecked Fleet
events.detail: The chapter closes with a summary of Jehoshaphat's twenty-five-year reign, noting the high places were never fully eliminated, before recording one final misstep: a shipbuilding alliance with wicked King Ahaziah of Israel that a prophet condemns in advance, and the ships are wrecked before they ever reach the sea.

verses.text: “Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, ‘Because you made an alliance with Ahaziah, the LORD will shatter what you have made.’ The ships were wrecked and unable to go to sea.”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · 2 Chronicles 21
eras.name: Jehoram's Evil Reign, and Elijah's Letter
eras.dates: David's dynasty nearly derails under Jehoram — a fratricide who marries into Ahab's family and receives a written condemnation from Elijah, one of only two places in Chronicles the prophet appears by name.

events.title: A Letter From Elijah, and an Agonizing Death
events.detail: Jehoram secures his throne by murdering all his brothers, marries Ahab's daughter, and leads Judah into the same apostasy as Israel; Elijah sends him a written prophecy of disaster, and Jehoram dies of a horrific intestinal disease after watching his own people plundered — buried without honor, and without a single mourner.

verses.text: “The LORD was unwilling to destroy David's dynasty because of the promise he had made to give David a perpetual dynasty.”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · 2 Chronicles 22-23
eras.name: Ahaziah, Athaliah's Massacre, and Joash Crowned
eras.dates: Ahab's bloodline nearly extinguishes David's entirely through Ahaziah's mother Athaliah, until a priest's wife hides one infant prince for six years and a coup led by his own family restores the throne.

events.title: Athaliah's Attempt to Destroy the Royal Line
events.detail: Ahaziah, corrupted by his mother Athaliah's counsel and killed alongside Ahab's family by Jehu, leaves his mother Athaliah to seize the throne by attempting to exterminate every remaining royal descendant — foiled only when Jehoshabeath, the high priest's wife, smuggles the infant Joash into hiding in the temple for six years.

verses.text: “When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she was determined to destroy the entire royal line of Judah.”

events.title: Jehoiada's Coup — Joash Crowned, Athaliah Executed
events.detail: In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest arms the temple guard, crowns the hidden boy-king Joash, and has Athaliah dragged out and executed rather than desecrate the temple with her death — after which the people demolish Baal's temple and restore proper worship.

eras.label: Era Twenty · 2 Chronicles 24
eras.name: Joash Repairs the Temple, Then Kills Zechariah
eras.dates: A king raised under a faithful priest's tutelage funds an entire temple renovation through a simple collection box, then, after that priest's death, has the priest's own prophet son stoned in the temple courtyard for daring to rebuke him.

events.title: The Collection Chest Outside the Gate
events.detail: Joash orders the Levites to collect temple-repair funds, and when they delay, institutes a simple chest by the gate that the people fill so consistently the temple is fully restored, with silver left over for new sacred implements.

events.title: Zechariah Stoned in the Temple Courtyard
events.detail: After Jehoiada's death, Joash abandons the LORD for Asherah poles and idols; when Jehoiada's own son Zechariah, empowered by God's Spirit, publicly rebukes the apostasy, Joash has him stoned to death in the temple courtyard — the very courtyard his father had once saved Joash's life in — and Zechariah's dying words ask the LORD to see and avenge it.

verses.text: “God's Spirit clothed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, ‘This is what God says: “Why are you transgressing the commandments of the LORD [Yahweh]? You will not prosper, for you have forsaken the LORD [Yahweh], and he has forsaken you.”’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · 2 Chronicles 25
eras.name: Amaziah's War and Idolatry
eras.dates: Amaziah obeys the law of Moses in sparing his father's assassins' sons, then imports the gods of the very people he just defeated — an inconsistency a prophet calls out to his face and pays for with a death threat.

events.title: Dismissing Mercenaries on a Prophet's Word
events.detail: Amaziah obeys the law of Moses by sparing his father's assassins' sons, then hires 100,000 Israelite mercenaries for his campaign against Edom — only to dismiss them at a prophet's warning that "the LORD is not with Israel," trusting God can give him "more than" the silver already paid.

verses.text: “Even if you go and fight bravely in battle, God will defeat you before the enemy. God is capable of helping or defeating.”

events.title: Worshiping the Gods of a Defeated Enemy
events.detail: Fresh from defeating Edom, Amaziah inexplicably adopts Edom's own gods and worships them; when a prophet asks why he worships gods that couldn't even save their own people, Amaziah threatens to kill him, then provokes and loses a humiliating war against Israel that ends with Jerusalem's wall broken down and Amaziah eventually assassinated in flight.

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · 2 Chronicles 26
eras.name: Uzziah's Pride and Leprosy
eras.dates: A genuinely capable, God-blessed king undoes his own long, successful reign in a single act of priestly overreach — entering the temple to burn incense himself, a role reserved exclusively for Aaron's descendants.

events.title: A Reign of Real Success
events.detail: Uzziah defeats the Philistines, receives tribute from Ammon, builds towers and cisterns, and fields an army of over 300,000 skilled warriors — succeeding, the text says, "as long as he followed the LORD."

events.title: "Once He Became Powerful, His Pride Destroyed Him"
events.detail: Uzziah enters the temple himself to burn incense, a role reserved for Aaron's priestly line alone; when eighty priests confront him, he becomes enraged, and a skin disease breaks out on his forehead on the spot — he lives out his remaining years quarantined and banned from the temple he desecrated.

verses.text: “But once he became powerful, his pride destroyed him. He disobeyed the LORD his God. He entered the LORD's temple to offer incense on the incense altar.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Three · 2 Chronicles 27
eras.name: Jotham's Faithful Reign
eras.dates: A brief, largely positive chapter credits Jotham's steady success directly to his determination to please the LORD — a rare uncomplicated reign sandwiched between his leprous father and his apostate son.

events.title: Building and Growing Powerful
events.detail: Jotham builds the temple's Upper Gate, fortifies cities, and defeats the Ammonites into paying heavy annual tribute, growing powerful "because he was determined to please the LORD his God" — though the text notes the people themselves "were still sinning."

verses.text: “Jotham grew powerful because he was determined to please the LORD his God.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Four · 2 Chronicles 28
eras.name: Ahaz's Apostasy, and an Ephraimite Act of Mercy
eras.dates: Ahaz's child sacrifice and total apostasy bring catastrophic military defeat, but the chapter's most striking scene is unique to Chronicles — Israelite soldiers themselves refusing to enslave captured Judahites, at a prophet's rebuke.

events.title: Defeat, Captivity, and an Unexpected Mercy
events.detail: Ahaz's child sacrifice and Baal worship bring disastrous defeats to Syria and Israel, with 120,000 Judahite warriors killed in a single day; when Israel's army returns with 200,000 captured women and children, the prophet Oded confronts them for planning to enslave their own brothers, and Ephraimite leaders release the captives, clothing and feeding them before sending them home.

verses.text: “Oded, a prophet of the LORD, was there… ‘You have killed them so mercilessly that God has taken notice. And now you are planning to enslave the people of Judah and Jerusalem. Yet are you not also guilty before the LORD your God? Send back those you have seized from your brothers, for the LORD is very angry at you!’”

events.title: Ahaz Closes the Temple
events.detail: Rather than turning to the LORD in his distress, Ahaz appeals to Assyria for help, sacrifices to the very gods of the nations defeating him, and finally shuts the doors of the LORD's temple entirely, erecting altars to other gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.

eras.label: Era Twenty-Five · 2 Chronicles 29
eras.name: Hezekiah Purifies the Temple
eras.dates: In the very first month of his reign, Hezekiah reopens his father's shuttered temple doors and launches an intensive sixteen-day purification, framing the restoration explicitly as a covenant renewal meant to turn back God's anger.

events.title: Reopening the Doors Ahaz Shut
events.detail: In the first month of his first year, Hezekiah reopens and repairs the temple doors his father closed, assembles the priests and Levites, and charges them to consecrate themselves and purify the sanctuary — a sixteen-day process that clears out every unclean item Ahaz had left inside.

verses.text: “My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD [Yahweh] has chosen you to stand in his presence, to minister to him, to be his ministers, and offer sacrifices.”

events.title: Sin Offerings and Restored Worship
events.detail: Hezekiah offers sin offerings for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and all Israel, restores David's musical arrangements for worship, and the people respond with such an overwhelming volume of voluntary sacrifices that the priests cannot skin all the animals fast enough without the Levites' help — the temple service reinstituted "quickly," to everyone's happiness.

eras.label: Era Twenty-Six · 2 Chronicles 30
eras.name: Hezekiah's Passover
eras.dates: Hezekiah reaches out even to the fallen northern kingdom with an invitation to a national Passover — mocked by most, but embraced by enough that Hezekiah prays God will simply forgive the many who came ceremonially unclean rather than turn them away.

events.title: An Invitation to All Israel
events.detail: Hezekiah sends letters throughout both Israel and Judah inviting everyone to a national Passover, appealing to those who survived Assyria's earlier deportations; most messengers are mocked and ridiculed, but some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humble themselves and come.

verses.text: “If you return to the LORD [Yahweh], your brothers and sons will be shown mercy by their captors and return to this land. The LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] is merciful and compassionate; he will not reject you if you return to him.”

events.title: "May the LORD, Who Is Good, Forgive"
events.detail: Because so many participants had not properly consecrated themselves, Hezekiah prays God would simply forgive those who came in good faith despite ceremonial impurity, and the LORD responds favorably; the celebration is extended a further seven days, producing joy in Jerusalem "unlike anything… since the time of King Solomon."

verses.text: “For Hezekiah prayed for them, saying: ‘May the LORD, who is good, forgive everyone who has determined to follow God, the LORD God of his ancestors, even if he is not ceremonially clean.’ The LORD responded favorably to Hezekiah and forgave the people.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Seven · 2 Chronicles 31
eras.name: Tithes and Provisions Organized
eras.dates: Overwhelming voluntary tithing floods the temple with so much surplus grain and produce that Hezekiah has to build entirely new storerooms just to hold it all.

events.title: Storerooms Overflowing With Tithes
events.detail: After destroying every remaining high place and Asherah pole, Hezekiah organizes priestly and Levitical divisions and calls for tithes to support them; the response is so overwhelming that new storerooms have to be built, and the priest Azariah reports "a large quantity left over" once everyone's needs were met.

verses.text: “Since the contributions began arriving in the LORD's temple, we have had plenty to eat and have a large quantity left over. For the LORD has blessed his people, and this large amount remains.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Eight · 2 Chronicles 32
eras.name: Sennacherib's Invasion, and Hezekiah's Prayer
eras.dates: Sennacherib's mocking siege letters, aimed straight at demoralizing Jerusalem's defenders, are answered not by Hezekiah's army but by a single angel — the same deliverance told in 2 Kings, framed here as the direct result of prayer.

events.title: "With Us Is the LORD Our God to Help Us"
events.detail: Facing Sennacherib's invasion, Hezekiah stops up the city's water supply, reinforces the walls, and rallies his officers with a simple contrast: Assyria has "mere human strength," but Judah has the LORD to fight their battles.

verses.text: “Be strong and brave! Don't be afraid and don't panic because of the king of Assyria… He has with him mere human strength, but the LORD our God is with us to help us and fight our battles!”

events.title: One Angel Against an Empire
events.detail: Sennacherib's messengers mock Hezekiah's trust in the LORD as no different from any other nation's futile trust in its own gods; Hezekiah and Isaiah pray together, and a single angel of the LORD wipes out the entire Assyrian army, sending Sennacherib home to be murdered by his own sons.

verses.text: “The LORD sent a messenger and he wiped out all the soldiers, princes, and officers in the army of the king of Assyria. So Sennacherib returned home humiliated. When he entered the temple of his god, some of his own sons struck him down with the sword.”

events.title: Hezekiah's Illness and Later Pride
events.detail: Healed from a terminal illness after prayer, Hezekiah later lets success go to his head and is tested by envoys from Babylon, though he and Jerusalem humble themselves again before his death — remembered overall as a king who "succeeded in all that he did."

eras.label: Era Twenty-Nine · 2 Chronicles 33
eras.name: Manasseh's Apostasy, and His Unexpected Repentance
eras.dates: The most idolatrous king in Judah's history — one who literally sets up altars inside the LORD's own temple — becomes, uniquely in Chronicles, the recipient of genuine mercy after being dragged to Babylon in chains and finally humbling himself.

events.title: Idols Inside the Temple Itself
events.detail: Manasseh rebuilds every high place his father destroyed, practices child sacrifice, sorcery, and necromancy, and — in an act with no real precedent — sets up idolatrous altars and images inside the LORD's own temple, in the very place God had said his name would dwell forever.

verses.text: “He put an idolatrous image he had made in God's [Elohim] temple, about which God [Elohim] had said to David and to his son Solomon, ‘This temple in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will be my permanent home.’”

events.title: Chains, Humility, and Restoration
events.detail: Assyrian commanders capture Manasseh, put hooks in his nose, and bind him in bronze chains to Babylon; in his suffering he genuinely humbles himself and pleads for mercy, and the LORD not only hears him but restores him to his throne in Jerusalem, where he spends his remaining years tearing down the very idols he had set up.

verses.text: “In his pain Manasseh asked the LORD [Yahweh] his God [Elohim] for mercy and truly humbled himself before the God of his ancestors. When he prayed to the LORD, the LORD responded to him… and brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom. Then Manasseh realized that the LORD [Yahweh] is the true God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Thirty · 2 Chronicles 34
eras.name: Josiah's Reforms, and the Law Scroll Found
eras.dates: Beginning to seek God as a teenager and purging idolatry as a young man, Josiah's mid-reign temple repairs uncover a forgotten scroll of the law whose contents terrify him into seeking a prophetic word about Judah's fate.

events.title: A Young King's Early Reforms
events.detail: Josiah begins seeking God at sixteen and purges idolatry throughout Judah and Israel by twenty, tearing down altars and burning the bones of pagan priests on their own altars before turning his attention to repairing the temple in his eighteenth year.

events.title: "I Found the Law Scroll" — Huldah's Oracle
events.detail: During temple repairs, Hilkiah discovers a forgotten scroll of the law; when it is read to Josiah, he tears his clothes in genuine alarm and sends officials to the prophetess Huldah, who confirms disaster is coming for Judah's idolatry but promises Josiah himself, because his heart was soft, will die in peace before he has to witness it.

verses.text: “Because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words concerning this place and its residents, and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Thirty-One · 2 Chronicles 35
eras.name: Josiah's Passover, and His Death at Megiddo
eras.dates: Josiah's Passover is remembered as unmatched since the prophet Samuel's own lifetime, making his sudden death soon after — ignoring a foreign king's warning that claimed to carry a word from God — all the more jarring.

events.title: A Passover Unmatched Since Samuel
events.detail: Josiah organizes an enormous, carefully prepared Passover celebration, personally supplying tens of thousands of animals from his own flocks; the text declares "a Passover like this had not been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet."

verses.text: “A Passover like this had not been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of the kings of Israel had observed a Passover like the one celebrated by Josiah.”

events.title: Death at Megiddo
events.detail: Necho of Egypt warns Josiah that he carries a message from God to hurry through unopposed, but Josiah disguises himself and engages him anyway at Megiddo, where archers mortally wound him; Jeremiah composes laments for him still sung "to this very day," and all Judah and Jerusalem mourn.

verses.text: “Josiah did not turn back from him; he disguised himself for battle. He did not take seriously the words of Necho that he had received from God; he went to fight him in the Plain of Megiddo.”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Two · 2 Chronicles 36
eras.name: The Last Kings, the Exile, and Cyrus's Decree
eras.dates: Four kings in rapid, tragic succession end the Davidic monarchy, and the book that opened with Solomon's temple closes with that same temple in ashes — yet ends, remarkably, on a note of hope: a pagan king's decree permitting the exiles to go home and rebuild.

events.title: Four Kings in Rapid Succession
events.detail: Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah each reign only briefly, each doing evil, as Egypt and then Babylon control Judah's throne; leading priests and people grow "more unfaithful," defiling the very temple the LORD had consecrated.

events.title: "There Was No One Who Could Prevent His Judgment"
events.detail: The LORD repeatedly sends warning through his messengers out of compassion for his people, but they mock and ridicule the prophets until judgment becomes unstoppable — Babylon's army slaughters without regard for age, burns the temple and the city, and Judah is deported until the land completes its sabbath rests, fulfilling Jeremiah's prophesied seventy years.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of their ancestors continually warned them through his messengers, for he felt compassion for his people… But they mocked God's [Elohim] messengers, despised his warnings, and ridiculed his prophets, until the rage of the LORD [Yahweh] came up against his people, until there was no healing.”

events.title: Cyrus's Decree — the Book's Final Word
events.detail: The Hebrew Bible's traditional final book ends not in despair but in hope: Cyrus of Persia, moved by the LORD, issues a decree permitting any of God's people to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple — the same decree that opens the book of Ezra.

verses.text: “This is what King Cyrus of Persia says: ‘The LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He has appointed me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Anyone of his people among you may go up there, and may the LORD [Yahweh] his God [Elohim] be with him.’”
